Here is a 300+ word summary of the Wikipedia page "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raymond_III,_Count_of_Tripoli" without commas and with 3 highlighted sections in markdown format:

Raymond III Count of Tripoli was lord of Sidon and count of Tripoli from 1147 until his death in 1183 he was a member of the House of Farners and the last count of Tripoli from this dynasty 
He succeeded his father Raymond II as count of Tripoli at a young age and was placed under the regency of his mother Helvisa of Jerusalem 
Raymond III played an important role in the politics of the Kingdom of Jerusalem during the reign of King Amalric I 

*highlighted section part 1* 
Raymond III was a key figure in the Second Crusade and later in the Crusades he was known for his military campaigns against the Muslim forces and his efforts to strengthen the Christian presence in the Levant 

Raymond III married Helvisa of Ibelin but the marriage was childless and he later married Maria of Antioch with whom he had no children either 
He was a close ally of the Byzantine Empire and supported the claims of Maria of Antioch to the throne of Jerusalem 
Raymond III was also known for his conflicts with the Knights Templar and the Knights Hospitaller 

*highlighted section part 2* 
The County of Tripoli under Raymond III was an important center of trade and culture the county was a major hub for the trade of spices and textiles and was known for its rich cultural heritage 

Raymond III died in 1183 without an heir and the county of Tripoli passed to his nephew Henry of Antioch 
He was remembered as a brave and wise leader who played an important role in the history of the Crusader states 

*highlighted section part 3* 
The legacy of Raymond III can be seen in the many castles and fortifications that he built during his reign these castles played an important role in the defense of the County of Tripoli against Muslim attacks 
Raymond III is also remembered for his efforts to promote Christianity in the Levant and for his support of the Christian churches in the region 
Despite his many achievements Raymond III is often overlooked in historical accounts of the Crusades
